heroHeadline: Day 696: Sheinbaum Details $5.8M García Luna-Linked Recovery for Guerrero Schools, Clarifies Fugitive Candidacy Rules, Pledges Ayotzinapa Report Ahead of Second Government Report
heroSubtitle: August 28, 2026 marks Day 696 of Claudia Sheinbaum's presidency, four days before her Second Government Report. UIF chief Omar Reyes Colmenares detailed a $5.8M recovery from the García Luna-linked Weinberg network — the first García Luna funds returned to the public purse, earmarked for schools in Guerrero's mountain region — as part of a UIF track record of 24,622 blocked accounts and 8.67 billion pesos frozen. Retired justice Arturo Zaldívar clarified that an arrest warrant alone doesn't bar a candidacy, only active fugitive status does, resolving ambiguity from the prior week's dual-nationality reform push tied to fugitive ex-governor Cabeza de Vaca. Sheinbaum met Ayotzinapa families, pledging a public report before the September 26 anniversary and pressing for Judge Ulises Bernabé's extradition. She said the economy is "doing well" despite U.S. tariffs, citing a 51% drop in daily homicides since September 2024 (86.9 → 42.5/day). This followed an August 26 signing of an overhaul to Mexico's 38-year-old core environmental law and an August 27 formal filing of the dual-nationality candidacy ban. Annual inflation ticked up to 3.26% in the first half of August (from 3.12% in July) but stayed within Banxico's target range; the peso continued trading near 16.9–17.0/USD, and approval held around 57% (Aug 6 AtlasIntel) as Banxico's policy rate stayed at 6.50%. No mañanera was held Saturday, August 29.
